prompt: The graph $y = -|x| + 7$ is a flipped, lifted V. What is the greatest $y$-value the graph ever reaches?
hint: The minus sign in front FLIPS the V upside down, so its point becomes the HIGHEST spot.

hints.text: The minus sign in front FLIPS the V upside down, so its point becomes the HIGHEST spot.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $y = -|x| + 1$. At $x = 0$ you get $y = 1$, and every other $x$ gives less. The top is 1. Same method here.
$|x|$ is never negative, so $-|x|$ is never above zero. The biggest it can be is $0$, when $x = 0$.
At $x = 0$: $y = -0 + 7 = 7$. That is the highest point.

explanation: $-f(x)$ flips the graph upside down over the $x$-axis, turning the V into an upside-down V.
The $+7$ lifts the whole flipped shape up 7.
The tip is now the top: at $x = 0$, $y = 7$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Try numbers on both sides
steps: At $x = 3$: $y = -3 + 7 = 4$. The values climb to 7 and then fall — 7 is the peak.
